name: Not Turning Back from the Two Spaces
previous_label: Urdhva Hastasana — Upward Salute (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: maruto 'ntar bahir vāpi viyadyugmānivartanāt | bhairavyā bhairavasyetthaṃ bhairavi vyajyate vapuḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
sanskrit_variants: Lakshmanjoo's edition (Manual for Self-Realization, as quoted by the Lakshmanjoo Academy) reads viyadyugmānuvartanāt ('by following / staying with the two spaces') where GRETIL, Singh and Wallis read viyadyugmānivartanāt ('by not turning back from the two spaces'). The practical sense (staying aware in the two pauses) is similar.
dharana.rendering: O Bhairavī, when the breath, whether it has moved inward or outward, is not hurried back from the two spaces where it comes to rest, the inner and the outer, then in this way Bhairava's form shows itself through Bhairavī.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh describes the two spaces as the split-second pauses at the heart-centre and at the outer dvādaśānta. Singh calls the two pauses the outer and inner kumbhaka but describes them as split-second natural pauses that are only observed; this school follows that observational reading.
dharana.technique_name: Not Turning Back from the Two Spaces

checked_against: Lakshmanjoo lineage: Lakshmanjoo Academy page quoting the Manual for Self-Realization labels verse 25 'Dhāraṇā 2'.
GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y1 (cont.) (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 25 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: inner space: where the in-breath rests (commentarial: heart-centre)
outer space: where the out-breath rests (commentarial: outer dvādaśānta)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The verse names a pair of spaces (viyad-yugma), one inside and one outside, where the breath pauses. The practice is to stay in each space a moment longer before attention rushes on.
geometry.svg_hint: two small open circles, one inside the chest and one in front of the nose, with the breath path looping between them
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Open the pause
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the breath cycle that felt hurried and continuous opens into two small spaces that are allowed to stay open. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: the quiet space after each in-breath and the quiet space after each out-breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Let each pause last exactly as long as it naturally lasts; do not lengthen it on purpose. Never force the pause.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Face the two spaces, and do not turn back from them too quickly
orientation.gravity: Body fully supported; nothing to hold up
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The two spaces where the breath rests, inside and outside
attention.secondary: The habit of rushing into the next breath, noticed and softened

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: O Bhairavī, when the breath, whether it has moved inward or outward, is not hurried back from the two spaces where it comes to rest, the inner and the outer, then in this way Bhairava's form shows itself through Bhairavī.
adiyogi.method_summary: Breathe naturally. Notice the small space after the in-breath and the small space after the out-breath. Stay present in each space instead of hurrying attention back into the next movement. Do not hold the breath to make the space longer.

honesty.disclosure: Door 002 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 2 (verse 25) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 002 is dharana 2, verse 25. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: Linking [retired posture] to VBT dharana 002 is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
legacy.notes: Serial school index pairs D-002 with method index 002. Shared experiential hook (breath-turn awareness) is a teaching braid only; editions also note verse-24/25 clustering as one breath-pause family.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Do not convert this into breath-holding. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: If standing overhead reach aggravates shoulders or low back, practice the same breath-pause attention seated with arms resting or only partially raised.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ease range if shoulders, neck, or low back complain; keep ribs soft and avoid forcing arms behind the ears.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 002: not turning back from the two spaces. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 2, verse 25.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat, or lie down. The map is a pair of spaces: one inside after the in-breath, one outside after the out-breath.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the body be fully held by the floor or chair. Eyes closed or lowered. Face the two spaces.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath, about four in and four out if you like to count. Never force the pause.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Stay present in the inner space and the outer space. Notice the urge to rush on, and let it soften.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a hurried cycle opens into two small spaces. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 25: by not turning back from the two spaces, inner and outer, Bhairava's form shows itself through Bhairavī. Do not hold the breath; just do not hurry away.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the breath go unwatched for one round. Open the eyes slowly.
